data.name: Diag_Intro
data.value:
Every row says whose problem it is. Data: references between entities that no longer resolve — fixed by opening an editor, and the row says which one. Schema: the database does not have the columns the code expects. Server: database server settings the application assumes and cannot enforce. Startup: a startup maintenance pass failed — the instance is running but did not start whole. Configuration: fixed outside the application. Source: the data arrives like this from IVAO — it cannot be fixed from here; it is known and watched, because it changes how much the resulting numbers can be trusted.

These are diagnoses only: this page changes no data. And ⚠️ if a check did not run, the absence of findings in its area does not mean all is well: a row says so explicitly.

data.name: Sf_Intro
data.value:
Two independent sources describe the same things: the IVAO API, where this site gets positions, frequencies, airports and runways from, and the division's Aurora sector file, written by IT-AOD. This page compares them.

It only says that they disagree: which one is right it does not know, and nothing is repaired from here. The fix belongs in the sector file, or in the IVAO data. The button at the bottom copies the list as text to send to whoever maintains the sector file.

The comparison runs by itself every 24 hours. Some of the differences are expected: the sector file is written before the AIRAC cycle takes effect, so it can be ahead. The ones that survive two cycles are not.

data.name: Struct_Fallback_Help
data.value:
Who takes this sector's traffic when it is offline. The rows below are read in order, and each one may apply only within an altitude band: the first row that applies and whose target is online takes the traffic. Once the rows run out, the fallback continues up the parent chain as it always did — which is why a sector with no rows behaves exactly as before.

It matters when the airspace split is vertical: with Milan split in two up to FL305 and a single sector open above, upper-east traffic goes to upper-west, not to lower-east, which is its parent.

⚠️ A transfer point that does not state an altitude cannot be resolved vertically: only rows without a band apply to it.

data.name: Apt_HelpBody
data.value:
Assignment of IVAO airports to ACCs: here you decide each airport's owning ACC, from which the sector hierarchy and the public page follow.

  • Auto-assign creates the airports whose owning ACC is already in the DB and imports their sectors from the source.
  • Re-import all re-fetches runways and Transition Altitude for every assigned airport: many calls in a row, progress is shown in the header and can be stopped.
  • Group actions (move, generate documents, delete, assign) work on the ticked rows; whatever fails stays selected.
  • An airport with no sectors stays hidden from the public until it generates its documents.

The page shares the lock of the structure pages: one person at a time.
